pages.intro: What a Wrights soft landscaping package covers, how it is priced, and how it is programmed against the rest of the works.

image.alt: Large planting scheme installed by Wrights Landscapes on a commercial project

blocks.html: Soft landscaping covers the living and organic elements of a scheme — topsoil, turf, seeding, shrubs, hedges, trees and mulch — as distinct from hard landscaping, which covers paving, kerbs, walls, fencing and surfacing.

Wrights Landscapes Group is a specialist soft landscaping contractor. We do not self-deliver hard landscaping, which means the package we price is the package we install, and it is priced by people who install it every week rather than by a generalist passing it down the chain.

We price from the landscape architect's drawings and specification, producing a bill of quantities broken down by plot, area or phase so that it can be checked line by line against the drawings and valued straightforwardly each month.

Where site conditions or supplied materials differ from specification — topsoil grade against BS 3882, nursery stock sizes against BS 3936, tree pit construction against BS 8545, seed mix composition against the NBS clause — we identify it and price it before works commence rather than after. That is usually the difference between a landscape package that closes out cleanly and one that ends up in dispute at the end of the maintenance period.

Soft landscaping sits at the end of the programme and is therefore the package most exposed to slippage upstream and to planting seasons. We work to the principal contractor's programme, flag season-critical activities early — bare-root planting windows, turf laying in high summer, seeding cut-offs — and phase works plot by plot where a development is handing over progressively.

pages.description: Soft landscaping subcontractor for national and regional housebuilders. Plot landscaping, show homes, communal areas and public open space across London, Hertfordshire and the South East.
pages.intro: Plot landscaping, show homes, sales areas, communal landscaping and public open space, delivered plot by plot to a housebuilder’s handover programme.

image.alt: Finished soft landscaping to a new-build home on a housebuilder development

blocks.html: Wrights Landscapes Group works as a soft landscaping subcontractor to national and regional housebuilders, delivering landscaping across whole developments from first show home through to final phase handover.

Housebuilder landscaping is a different discipline from one-off commercial landscaping. The work is repetitive, it is measured plot by plot, it has to fit around sales, snagging and customer care, and it is almost always the last trade on a plot before handover. We are set up for that: multiple gangs, plot-by-plot valuation, and a customer care function that responds to post-occupation issues without a separate procurement exercise each time.

blocks.text: What we deliver on a development

items.title: Plot landscaping
items.html: Front and rear garden landscaping to individual plots: topsoil placement and grading, turfing, seeding, shrub and hedge planting, bed formation, mulching and edging, sequenced to the handover programme.

items.title: Show homes and sales areas
items.html: Enhanced landscaping to show homes, sales suites and marketing areas, where finish standards and timescales are tighter than standard plots and the work is under public view from the day it is completed.

items.title: Communal and apartment landscaping
items.html: Landscaping to shared courtyards, car park surrounds, bin and cycle store surrounds, entrance areas and communal gardens on apartment blocks.

items.title: Public open space
items.html: Larger amenity areas, POS, attenuation basin and swale planting, buffer planting, structure planting and play area surrounds, usually with adoption or management company requirements attached.

items.title: Biodiversity and ecology works
items.html: Wildflower turf and species-rich seeding, native hedgerow and whip planting, and habitat planting delivered to meet biodiversity net gain conditions and ecological clerk of works requirements.

items.title: Maintenance and customer care
items.html: Twelve- and twenty-four-month maintenance periods, watering, replacement planting and defect rectification, plus responsive customer care visits to occupied plots.

blocks.html: On a live housing development the constraint is rarely the landscaping itself — it is getting clean access to a plot in the right week, in the right season, with the levels right and the arisings gone. We plan around that: weekly plot releases, advance notice of what we need from groundworks, and honest advice about which plots should wait for a planting season rather than being turfed in August and replaced in November.

We work on JCT and NEC subcontract forms and are familiar with application-for-payment, payment notice and pay-less notice procedures under the Construction Act. We provide plot-by-plot measurement to support monthly valuation, retention release and final account agreement.

pages.title: Large-Scale Planting & Commercial Tree Planting Contractors | Wrights Landscapes Group
pages.description: Large-scale planting and commercial tree planting contractors. Bulk shrub planting, standard and semi-mature trees, tree pits, staking and establishment across London, Hertfordshire and the South East.
pages.h1: Large-scale planting and commercial tree planting
pages.intro: Bulk shrub and hedge planting, standard and semi-mature tree planting, tree pit construction and establishment on construction projects.

image.alt: Commercial soft landscaping and planting project in Hertfordshire

blocks.html: Wrights Landscapes Group has the labour, procurement and nursery supply network required to deliver large-scale commercial planting and tree-planting schemes to programme, including semi-mature stock and season-critical bare-root works.

Volume planting is a procurement problem as much as a labour one. Getting three thousand shrubs and two hundred trees of the right species, size and form onto a site in the right week, in condition, is where these packages succeed or fail. We hold relationships with nurseries in the UK and across Europe and place orders early enough to reserve stock rather than take whatever is left in the planting season.

items.title: Shrub and herbaceous planting
items.html: Bulk planting to landscape architects' schedules and setting-out drawings, including bed preparation, soil amelioration, planting to density, mulching and weed-control fabric where specified.

items.title: Standard and semi-mature trees
items.html: Planting from light standard through to semi-mature and extra-heavy standard stock, with lifting and handling planned for access, including root-balled, containerised and bare-root supply.

items.title: Tree pits and support systems
items.html: Tree pit excavation and construction to specification, including tree pit substrates, root barriers, aeration and irrigation systems, underground guying, above-ground staking and tying, and tree grilles or guards.

items.title: Hedgerow and native whip planting
items.html: Native hedgerow, whip and transplant planting for boundary, screening and habitat purposes, including guards, canes and mulching, delivered within the bare-root season.

items.title: Structure and buffer planting
items.html: Woodland edge, buffer, screening and structure planting to public open space and development margins, typically at higher densities and to ecological or planning-condition specifications.

items.title: Establishment and replacement
items.html: Watering regimes, formative pruning, stake and tie adjustment, failure inspection and replacement planting through the defects and maintenance period.

blocks.html: We plant to BS 8545 (trees from nursery to independence in the landscape), BS 3936 (nursery stock), BS 4428 (general landscape operations) and BS 3882 (topsoil), and to project-specific NBS clauses where these are more onerous. Where a specification cannot be met with the stock available in a given season, we say so in writing before ordering and propose an equivalent for the landscape architect's approval rather than substituting quietly.

Bare-root and root-balled planting is a winter operation, broadly November to March. Container-grown stock extends the window but at higher cost and with a heavier watering liability through establishment. Where a programme pushes planting outside its proper season we will price it, but we will also set out the failure risk and the additional watering requirement so that the liability is understood by everyone before the works start.

pages.title: Commercial Turfing, Seeding & Wildflower Landscaping | Wrights Landscapes Group
pages.description: Commercial turf installation, amenity grass seeding, wildflower turf and species-rich seed mixes for biodiversity net gain, for housebuilders and main contractors across London, Hertfordshire and the South East.
pages.intro: Turf installation, amenity grass seeding, wildflower turf and species-rich seeding, including full ground preparation and establishment.

image.alt: Newly laid commercial turf on a Wrights Landscapes project

blocks.html: Wrights Landscapes Group provides commercial turfing, wildflower turf, amenity and species-rich seeding, and the ground preparation that determines whether any of it establishes.

Most turf and seeding failures are ground preparation failures. Compacted subsoil, construction arisings left in the profile, topsoil placed too thin or too wet, or levels that pond — these show up six weeks after handover, not on the day. We price the preparation properly and record the ground conditions we take over.

items.title: Commercial turf installation
items.html: Cultivated amenity turf to plots, communal areas, public open space and commercial grounds, laid to specification with joints staggered and closed, rolled and firmed, and watered in.

items.title: Ground preparation
items.html: Subsoil ripping and decompaction, removal of construction arisings, topsoil supply, placement and grading to specified depths, stone picking, amelioration and pre-turfing fertiliser.

items.title: Amenity grass seeding
items.html: Seeding to amenity and low-maintenance mixes for larger areas, including hydroseeding where access or gradient requires it, with establishment cuts through to sward closure.

items.title: Wildflower turf
items.html: Wildflower turf to specified species mixes for instant establishment on biodiversity, public open space and attenuation areas where seeding timescales or slope stability make turf the better option.

items.title: Species-rich and biodiversity seeding
items.html: Native and species-rich seed mixes to meet biodiversity net gain conditions, ecological requirements and planning conditions, sown to specified rates within the correct sowing window.

items.title: Establishment and aftercare
items.html: Watering regimes, establishment cutting, overseeding of bare patches, weed control and replacement through the maintenance period.

blocks.html: Turf laid in July and August will die without water. That is not a workmanship question, it is a physical one, and it becomes a commercial question about who is responsible for watering and who is paying for it. We set the watering liability out clearly at tender stage — who waters, how often, from what supply, and what happens if the site water is turned off — because leaving it implicit is the most common cause of argument on a landscaping package.

pages.title: Commercial Grounds Maintenance Contractors | Wrights Landscapes Group
pages.description: Grounds maintenance and landscape aftercare for developments, managing agents and estates. Twelve and twenty-four month maintenance periods, watering regimes, defect rectification and replacement planting.
pages.intro: Maintenance periods, watering regimes, defect rectification and ongoing grounds maintenance contracts, through our Grounds Maintenance Division.

image.alt: Landscaped grounds on a completed housing development maintained by Wrights Landscapes

blocks.html: Wrights Landscapes Group operates a separate Grounds Maintenance Division covering contractual maintenance periods on our own installations and standalone grounds maintenance contracts for developments, estates and commercial sites.

A landscape scheme is signed off at practical completion but judged twelve or twenty-four months later. The maintenance period is where planting either establishes or is replaced at somebody's cost, so it is worth pricing and programming as seriously as the installation.

items.title: Contractual maintenance periods
items.html: Twelve- and twenty-four-month maintenance periods on installed schemes: grass cutting, watering, weeding, mulch topping up, formative pruning, stake and tie adjustment, and scheduled inspections with written records.

items.title: Watering regimes
items.html: Programmed watering of trees, shrubs and turf through establishment, by bowser or from site supply, with visit records so that the regime can be evidenced if failures are later disputed.

items.title: Defect rectification and replacement
items.html: Inspection for failures, identification of cause, and replacement planting to the original specification, with clear separation between establishment failure, specification failure and damage by others.

items.title: Ongoing grounds maintenance
items.html: Scheduled maintenance contracts for completed developments, managing agents, management companies, housing associations and commercial estates: grass cutting, hedge cutting, bed maintenance, litter picking and seasonal works.

items.title: Customer care
items.html: Responsive visits to occupied plots on housebuilder developments, dealing with landscaping items raised through customer care within the defects period.

items.title: Renovation and reinstatement
items.html: Bringing neglected or failed landscaping back into condition: scarification, aeration, overseeding, bed clearance, replacement planting and re-mulching.

blocks.html: Every maintenance visit is recorded. When a tree fails eighteen months after planting, the question is always whether it was the stock, the pit, the watering or the weather. Dated visit records and photographs settle that quickly and keep it from becoming a commercial dispute at final account.

pages.intro: A specialist soft landscaping subcontractor, built since 2016 around repeat work for housebuilders and main contractors.

image.alt: Completed planting and turfing to a new-build plot by Wrights Landscapes

blocks.html: Wrights Landscapes Group Ltd is a commercial soft landscaping subcontractor based in Stevenage, Hertfordshire. The company was founded in 2016 by managing director Ed Wright and works across London, Hertfordshire and the South East of England.

We install and maintain the soft landscaping element of construction projects: plot and garden landscaping on housing developments, public open space and communal landscaping, large-scale planting and tree planting, commercial turfing and seeding, podium and roof planting, and the maintenance periods that follow. We work business-to-business, as a subcontractor, and we do not undertake domestic garden work.

The business has grown on repeat work. Most of what we do in a given year is for clients we worked for the year before, which is the only durable way to build a subcontracting business and the reason we would rather flag a specification problem at tender stage than discover it at final account.

We run our own directly employed operatives rather than working purely through labour-only supply, which is what allows us to hold multiple concurrent sites and to respond to plot releases at short notice. Procurement runs through established nursery and turf supply relationships in the UK and across Europe, which matters most when a programme calls for volume stock in a busy planting season.
A separate Grounds Maintenance Division handles maintenance periods, aftercare and standalone maintenance contracts, so that establishment works are not competing for resource with installation.

Wrights Landscapes Group is Constructionline Gold and CHAS accredited. We work under principal contractors' site rules and CDM 2015 duties, provide project-specific RAMS, and can supply full PQQ documentation, insurance certificates, method statements and training records on request.

items.q: Who does soft landscaping for housebuilders in Hertfordshire?
items.a: Wrights Landscapes Group Ltd, based in Stevenage, is a commercial soft landscaping subcontractor working for national housebuilders and main contractors across Hertfordshire, London and the South East. The company has operated since 2016 and is Constructionline Gold and CHAS accredited.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes undertake commercial landscaping?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes Group is a commercial landscaping contractor specialising in soft landscaping for the construction industry, working as a subcontractor to housebuilders and main contractors. It does not undertake domestic garden work.

Wrights Landscapes is based in Stevenage, Hertfordshire and works throughout Hertfordshire, Greater London, Essex, Bedfordshire, Buckinghamshire, Cambridgeshire, Northamptonshire, Kent, Surrey and the wider South East of England.

items.q: What is soft landscaping in construction?
items.a: Soft landscaping covers the living and organic elements of a scheme: topsoil, turf, seeding, shrubs, hedges, trees and mulch. It is distinct from hard landscaping, which covers paving, kerbs, walls, fencing and surfacing. On a construction project soft landscaping is usually let as a separate subcontract package towards the end of the programme.

items.q: What is the difference between soft and hard landscaping contractors?
items.a: Soft landscaping contractors deliver planting, turfing and seeding. Hard landscaping contractors deliver paving, walling, fencing and surfacing. Many schemes let the two as separate packages. Wrights Landscapes Group specialises in soft landscaping and associated grounds maintenance.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes work with housebuilders?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes undertakes plot landscaping, show homes and sales areas, communal landscaping and wider public open space landscaping for national and regional housebuilders, sequenced to the handover programme.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes work as a subcontractor to main contractors?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes Group works as a subcontractor under principal contractors and housebuilders on both JCT and NEC subcontract forms, and is familiar with application-for-payment, payment notice and pay-less notice procedures under the Construction Act.

items.q: Can Wrights Landscapes undertake large planting schemes?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes has the labour, procurement and nursery supplier network required to deliver large-scale commercial planting and tree-planting schemes, including standard and semi-mature trees, tree pit construction, staking and establishment.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes provide commercial turfing?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes provides commercial turf installation, wildflower turf, amenity grass seeding, species-rich and biodiversity seeding, and the associated ground preparation and establishment works.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes carry out biodiversity net gain planting?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes installs wildflower turf, species-rich and native seed mixes, native hedgerow and whip planting and habitat planting to meet biodiversity net gain conditions and ecological requirements on development sites.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes provide maintenance after practical completion?
items.a: Yes. The Grounds Maintenance Division carries out twelve- and twenty-four-month maintenance periods, watering regimes, defect rectification and replacement planting, as well as standalone grounds maintenance contracts for completed developments and estates.

items.q: Is Wrights Landscapes Constructionline and CHAS accredited?
items.a: Yes. Wrights Landscapes Group is Constructionline Gold and CHAS accredited, and can supply full PQQ documentation, RAMS, insurance certificates and method statements on request.

items.q: How does Wrights Landscapes price a soft landscaping package?
items.a: Wrights prices from the landscape architect's drawings and specification, producing a bill of quantities broken down by plot, area or phase. Where site conditions or supplied materials fall outside specification, this is identified and priced before works commence rather than after.

items.q: What size projects does Wrights Landscapes take on?
items.a: Soft landscaping packages across single-phase and multi-phase residential developments, commercial sites and public realm schemes, with the capacity to hold several concurrent sites.

items.q: Does Wrights Landscapes do domestic garden work?
items.a: No. Wrights Landscapes Group works business-to-business only, as a subcontractor to housebuilders, main contractors, groundworks contractors, housing associations and estate managers.
